visualComparisons.observation: NJB-300 has visibly heavier strokes than NPN-030, narrower 0 counters and a comparatively tighter, heavier 3. NPN-030 has lighter strokes, larger 0 openings and a more open rounded 3. Both share the flag base, but their serial alphabets must not be collapsed solely by base or year. The source explicitly assigns NJB to non-passenger tooling and NPN to Classic.
visualComparisons.method: Visual inspection of original photographs in contact sheet; no outline trace, perspective normalization or numerical contour certification.

visualComparisons.observation: The D0-0909 dealer photograph has tall narrow rounded-rectangular 0 bowls with long straight sides and heavier paint shoulders, visually closer to NJB-300 than the lighter NPN-030 Classic example. This supports a non-passenger tooling comparison across passenger and dealer classes. Wear, cropping and paint spread differ; dealer subtype and complete alphabet identity remain provisional.
visualComparisons.method: Visual inspection of original photographs in contact sheet; no outline trace, perspective normalization or numerical contour certification.

visualComparisons.observation: The 0 on 7520-GD has a tall straight-sided bowl and rounded ends; its relatively light strokes resemble the NPN-030 Classic 0 more closely than the heavy NJB-300/dealer examples. The rounded open 5 and narrow strokes on GD also show that commercial class alone does not imply one heavy narrow non-passenger alphabet. Source identifies this side of the GD/GF bracket as Astrographic; assigning every glyph specifically to Classic requires more matched specimens.
visualComparisons.method: Visual inspection of original photographs in contact sheet; no outline trace, perspective normalization or numerical contour certification.

visualComparisons.observation: 9955-GF visibly differs from 7520-GD: the repeated 9 has round open bowls and long sweeping diagonal tails, and the 5 has a broad rounded lower bowl. These are coherent repeated shapes within GF. Their broader open construction contrasts with the more condensed GD alphabet. The source independently brackets the maker transition between GD and GF; decal labels 2003/2005 are not used as proof of manufacture date.
visualComparisons.method: Visual inspection of original photographs in contact sheet; no outline trace, perspective normalization or numerical contour certification.

visualComparisons.observation: 836-DKW and B31-865 both display round open 8 counters with a continuous narrowed waist and a sweeping 6 diagonal into a large lower bowl. The 5 on B31-865 and 9955-GF has a similar broad lower bowl and flat top stroke. Their photographed forms support a Waldale family comparison across passenger, collector and commercial plates. Layout, size and black/blue paint differ; no claim that the whole alphabet or physical tool size is identical.
visualComparisons.confidence: manufacturer-family similarity supported; full alphabet/tool identity unconfirmed
